notes_summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on precise latency SLO definitions (p50/p95/p99) across streaming vs non-streaming, alignment on client- vs server-side timing, and reserved GPU sizing for predictable throughput.
notes:
Context: Stratus is the payments platform for 120M annual transactions; strict latency targets for fraud scoring and support chat. They want Dedicated for predictable tail behavior and Private for residency.

Key ask: Define SLOs in measurable terms that both sides can instrument and audit. They are sensitive to p99 tail, want streaming-first experience for support chat, and want clear reserved GPU planning for peak windows.

Measurement specifics discussed:
- SLO targets proposed by Stratus: non-streaming inference p50 < 40ms, p95 < 90ms, p99 < 250ms for 256-token sequences; streaming first-byte p95 < 35ms, per-chunk p95 < 20ms, p99 tail < 300ms.
- Redwood recommendation: canonicalize on server-side "inference start" and "inference end" timestamps (server wall-clock), plus client-side SDK metrics for RTT (DNS/TCP/TLS/TTFB/last_byte). Agree to both sets for cross-validation.
- Define warm vs cold start: exclude requests that trigger model load (cold) from SLO windows; keep separate cold-start SLA. Use synthetic pre-warm probes to avoid load-induced cold starts during peak.
- Streaming vs non-streaming alignment: streaming SLOs measured on first-byte latency (time to first token) and chunk latency (time between consecutive token batches). Non-streaming measured end-to-end server compute + queue time.
- Sampling strategy: production sampling of 1% of live traffic + full synthetic bench at 5x expected peak for acceptance. Require >=10k samples per day for stable p99 estimates during evaluation.

Reserved GPU planning & throughput guarantees:
- Stratus expects Reserved capacity to cover 95th percentile peak traffic for payment-fraud flows and 99th for support chat during promotions. Initial ask: reserve 8x A100 80GB equivalents in a single region for low-latency routing.
- Redwood to produce sizing matrix: requests/sec per GPU for common sequence lengths (64/256/512 tokens), expected tokens/sec, and memory headroom for KV cache. Early estimate from Redwood: 1x A100 -> ~120 non-streaming 256-token reqs/sec at p95 target; so 8 GPUs -> ~960 reqs/sec sustained. Need to validate with perf run.
- Throughput guarantees: target committed throughput window with burst allowance (+25%) and transparent throttling policy. Stratus requires priority routing to dedicated pool during peak.

SLA negotiation points:
- Measurement authority: Redwood will publish server-side logs and per-request telemetry; Stratus requires filtered, redacted access to these logs and periodic summary exports for audit.
- Remedies for missed SLOs: credits vs escalation playbook; Stratus pushing for higher credit % for p99 misses.
- Maintenance windows: Stratus requests limited disruptive maintenance windows and multi-zone redundancy guarantees.

POC / acceptance criteria for evaluation:
- Performance run simulating 5x peak for 30 minutes with p95/p99 within agreed tolerances.
- End-to-end traceability: every sampled request must have client- and server-timestamps for reconciliation.
- Security: pass Stratus security questionnaire items 1-42, SOC2 report provided, KMS integration test.

- 2026-02-25: Intro call with Jordan, Priya. High-level requirements captured (FF-2026-02-25-023).
- 2026-03-01: Deep-dive on latency measurements with infra + SRE (FF-2026-03-01-117). Agreed to draft measurement spec.

Open items / blockers:
- Need mutual definition of exactly which network components are included in "client-side" vs "server-side" timing for billing/credit triggers.
- Security questionnaire answers pending (SEC-1012).
- CFO wants 6-month trial before full ARR commit; impacts reserved capacity term negotiation.

- Draft SLA with concrete credit bands for p95 and p99 misses; targeted delivery 2026-03-22.
